newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea won ends up, rebounds from all-time low.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea won ends up, rebounds from all-time low.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the dollar on Tuesday, bouncing back up from the morning's all-time low after the central bank intervened twice to sell dollars, traders said.
But the bank declined to confirm the moves as it regularly does. The won ended at 897.60, compared with Monday's closing of 898.70. It opened weak at 898.90 on dollar short-covering and import deals.
The central bank stepped in for the first time shortly after the won hit the new historical low of 901.00, traders said.
It came in again in the afternoon, bringing down the intervention level to 899.80 from the morning's 900.00, they said.
Traders said the central bank's firm intention to keep the dollar below the 900 level would prevent much dollar buying on Wednesday.
"The 900 level is viewed by the central bank as an absolute level that should not be broken," a local trader said.
The mid-rate is seen at 899.30 on Wednesday, compared with 897.50 on Tuesday.
